To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the vacuum polarization tensor satisfies BRS invariance with respect to the gauge-fixing vector n, (ii) the vacuum polarization satisfies BRS in invariance with resect to the gauge-fixin vector n′, and (iii) the vacuum polarization is UV finite in the limit η→0.
the UV-divergent contribution to the one-loop vacuum polarization tensor satisfies BRS invariance with respect to the gauge fixing vectors n and n′.

the UV-divergent one-loop contribution to a Green function satisfies BRS identities governing the dependence on gauge-fixing parameters, that these identities cannot be obtained within a pragmatic approach to a generalized LM prescription and that a BRS-invariance of the generalized LM prescription provides a way to obtain the identities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a BRS-invariance proof of the LM prescription.
a study of BRS symmetry in the presence of a generalized gauge fixing and its application to the LM prescription of gauge fixing.
the BRS invariance of the LM prescription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BRS identities provide a rigorous proof of the gauge-independence of the one-loop Green functions.
the BRS identities for the n′-dependence are satisfied in the LM prescription.
the n and n′ dependences of the gauge-fixing functions and of the vacuum polarization tensor satisfy the BRS identity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the BRS identities are a useful tool for the study of gauge fixing.
we have been able to establish the BRS identities for the vacuum polarization tensor and the Green functions in general for the temporal gauge.
the n′ dependence of the Green functions is a consequence of BRS invariance and the n dependence is a consequence of the BRS identities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BRS symmetry of gauge theories is a very powerful tool to study the n and n′ dependence of gauge theory observables.
the BRS identities are a powerful tool for studying the gauge dependence of the Green functions.
the BRS symmetry is a powerful tool to understand and control the dependence of Green functions on auxiliary parameters introduced in a gauge fixing.
